[2026-09-21] rc:4066452749 inline on src/validation.cpp by fjahr (member):
Ok, I understand the rationale better now. I think part of my issue with the class and "x has type Y" is that it's just used temporarily and `flags` is converted back to a plain `script_verify_flags` on return, so nothing outside the function learns anything from the type. If the class was globally used I would say "x only takes values from Y" is really visibly true. The way it is used now it really functions just like a `static_assert` which seems at least unusual to me.

I experimented a bit and ended up with an alternative using `static_assert` that is simpler and feels more expressive to me: https://github.com/fjahr/bitcoin/commit/0dcd33087fcfd580d3a1d847a59218f01ed8cd93 What do you think?

It deduplicates the basic and buried deployments so it touches more of the existing code and it also needs a bit of extra code for new deployments since these are a third category aside from basic and buried. After having gone through this exercise I am also a bit more sympathetic to the current approach but if those trade-offs were the drivers for the approach here it wasn't clear to me before.
</new_statements>
